questions.prompt: minidsh runs in a CI job with no terminal attached and policy ask. The model calls run_command. What outcome does askPerson return?
options: unavailable, because there is no terminal and nobody can answer
cancelled, because the job will end
It waits until someone types an answer
questions.explanation: With no terminal, nobody can answer, so the outcome is unavailable, which the listener treats as a denial.

questions.prompt: You answer "yes please" at the [y/N] prompt. What happens?
options: The call runs, because the answer starts with y
The call is denied, because only exactly y counts as a grant
The call runs once and future calls are allowed too
questions.explanation: Anything other than a clear y is rejected. Requiring an exact yes means a typo or a vague answer never allows a risky action.

questions.prompt: Why does the denial message tell the model to stop and explain instead of working around it?
options: Without it, the model may try the same action through a different tool
Because the model cannot read the outcome name
Because the pipeline requires every error to be two sentences
So the person gets asked a second time
questions.explanation: A model told only that a call failed may look for another route to the same goal. Saying the person refused, and what to do instead, stops that.
